title: High gas-to-dust size ratio indicating efficient radial drift in the mm-faint CX Tauri disk
question: How compact is the mm dust disk of CX Tau relative to its CO gas disk, and does it show substructure, indicating radial drift?

data.sensitivity: 20.3 uJy/beam continuum; 4.4 mJy/beam per 0.1 km/s channel CO

evidence.quote: The dynamical estimate for the mass of the star is $0.31\,M_\odot$
they found that the typical ratio is $1.96$, with a standard error on the mean of $0.04$
The unresolved spectral index between 1 and 3  mm is $2.3$

recipe.method: Azimuthally symmetric two-component intensity profile fitted in uv-plane with GALARIO and MCMC
key_parameters: 90 walkers, 18000 steps after 2000 burn-in; uniform priors

recipe.method: Curve of growth in elliptical apertures from moment maps/images using continuum inclination, PA and center
Mid-plane temperature profile from stellar luminosity, then invert I = B(T)(1-exp(-tau)) using the best-fit model
Add R_trunc to the intensity profile and refit with 100 walkers; upper limit from 95% of MC realizations

evidence.quote: The derived integrated flux density is $9.75\pm0.12\,$mJy
The radius enclosing 68% of the continuum flux density is $14.0\pm0.3\,$AU
The integrated flux of the line is $1937\pm54\,$mJy km s$^{-1}$
The radius enclosing $68\%$ of the $^{12}$CO $J$=2-1 flux is $75\pm$5 AU.
At the $68\%$ enclosing flux radius the ratio of $R_{\rm gas}$ to $R_{\rm dust}\approx5.4$
while at the $90\%$ enclosing flux radius the ratio is $\approx3.9$
with an upper limit on $R_{\rm trunc}$ of $0.54\,$AU
